Ἢ γὰρ ὅτι ἄνθρωπος ὢν ὁ Χριστὸς, τὰ ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπου λαλήσει φύσιν, καὶ οὐχὶ μόνοις ἐμμενεῖ τοῖς τῆς κενώσεως μέτροις, διά γε τὸ εἶναι Θεὸς καὶ ἐκ Θεοῦ κατὰ φύσιν. «Ἐγὼ γὰρ, ἔφασκε, καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἕν ἐσμεν,» καὶ, «Ὁ ἑωρακὼς ἐμὲ, ἑώρακε τὸν Πατέρα.» Ἢ ἐκεῖνό που τάχα· γινώσκεται γὰρ ἄνωθεν τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου καὶ τῶν Χερουβὶμ, τουτέστιν, ἐν ὑπεροχῇ καὶ δόξῃ τῇ ὑπὲρ ἄνθρωπον, καὶ παντὸς ἐπέκεινα γενητοῦ, ὧν τὸ ἀκρότατόν τε καὶ ὑπέρτατον τὰ Σεραφὶμ, εἰ καὶ γέγονε σάρξ. Ἐκ χρυσοῦ δὲ τὸ ἱλαστήριον, καὶ αὐτὰ τὰ Σεραφίμ. Ἡ μὲν γὰρ εὐκλεής τε καὶ περικαλλεστάτη φύσις, Θεός. Ἐν ὁμοιώσει δὲ τῇ πρὸς αὐτὸν κατὰ μέθεξιν, τὰ γενητά. Τοῖς δὲ ἐν κύκλῳ καὶ ἀγχοῦ γεγονόσιν αὐτοῦ, τὴν τῆς ἰδίας καὶ φυσικῆς φαιδρότητος ἐπιμερίζει μέθεξιν, ὡς φωτὸς ἐπί τι τῶν πέλας ἀντανακλωμένου, καὶ λαμπρότητι τῇ ἰδίᾳ τὸ προστυχὸν καταυγάζοντος.

pass_a_gloss: …leitourgika pneumata / ministering spirits… egō kai ho Patēr hen / I and the Father one… trapezan / table… artous enōpious / face-breads… artos ex ouranou / bread from heaven…
pass_b_english: Cyril: …spirits sent unto service because of those about to inherit salvation.’ And from above the mercy-seat I will be known to you, he says, and I will speak to you, somehow showing two things, as I at least think, also through this. For either that Christ, being human, will speak the things beyond human nature, and will not remain only in the measures of the emptying, because of being God and from God by nature. ‘For I,’ he was saying, ‘and the Father are one,’ and, ‘The one who has seen me has seen the Father.’ Or perhaps that; for he is known from above the mercy-seat and the cherubim—that is, in superiority and glory beyond human, and beyond every generated thing, of which the Seraphim are the most extreme and highest—even if he became flesh. And from gold is the mercy-seat, and the Seraphim themselves. For the well-famed and most beautiful nature is God. And in likeness toward him according to participation are the generated. And to those who have become in a circle and near him he distributes a share of his own and natural brightness, as of light being reflected upon something of those near, and illuminating with its own brightness what happens upon it.
Palladius: The word holds uprightly for us, and has been polished unto the true.

Cyril: And after the construction of the mercy-seat, he also sketches for us the mystery of Christ otherwise, saying: ‘And you will make a table of pure gold.’ And having ordered that rings must have been fixed to it, and the gold carriers cast in, and having said most clearly the measures of it and the modes of good craft according to which it would become having obtained the conspicuous unto the uppermost form, ‘And you will set,’ he says, ‘upon the table face-breads before me through all.’ And he has commanded its vessels to become gold—bowls and censers, and indeed also ladles and drink-offering cups. Was not the bread from heaven clearly being shown to us, about to lie forward according to times upon holy tables of churches, and giving life to the world?

Cyril: Bowls and censers, ladles and drink-offering cups, and the things through which the mystical and most holy need of the holy table is fulfilled—would they not be a type of the divine treasures, O friend?

Cyril: But these things in Exodus. And concerning table and indeed also setting-forward of breads the lawgiver has oracled in Leviticus; and he somehow widens the commandment, and teaches clearly in what manner the setting-forward will be, saying thus: ‘And you will take fine flour, and you will make it twelve breads. Two tenths will be the one bread. And you will set them two settings, and six breads the one setting upon the pure table before the Lord. And you will set upon the setting pure frankincense and salt, and they will be unto breads unto a remembrance lying forward for the Lord; on the day of the sabbaths
